* start a citizen deputy program, enlisting volunteers from within the community * Provide police training in deescalation techniques, etc. * Have local police provide oversight and work closely with the citizen deputies * Watch crime plummet

In other words, take the local parent / community watchdog groups and enable them to assist in policing. End police brutality and increase effectiveness through local citizen deputies

It seems that there's an inverse relationship between the amount of things you have and the attention you pay to each one. This makes sense of course, since the time in a day is constant. However, we should develop on some level an appreciation and relationship with the things in our life. You should consider this relationship more like one of the pantheist / naturalist 'grateful' type of relationship, i.e., we recognize the value a certain object provides in our lives, e.g., our favorite jacket keeps us warm, a nice pair of headphones let us enjoy good music, &c. Notice how this is more at 'reverent' and less at 'adoration'; materialism is a dangerous trapping and will actually, ironically, lead us to appreciate less the items in our lives.

SO! All this preamble as a sort of context: give these items in your life a proper home. If you asked me where anything was in my house, I would be able to tell you rather precisely where such item is. This is a simple as books belonging in a bookcase, or documents and paperwork in a filing cabinet (not in kitchen drawers, people)- that's all it really boils down to. But you are actually doing more than meets the eye when you give something a place to live: you are mentally determining how this object fits into your life, conceptually. Having difficulty providing an item with a residence might be indicative of us not understanding that item's role in our lives; indeed, it may just be sentimental at this point.

More practically, however, this exercise accomplishes something I love: it removes unnecessary mental effort from our lives. Where did I put my keys? Where they always go. Where are 2012's tax returns? Where all paperwork is (and hopefully it is more organized than that!). In this way, you can remove the stress of trying to track down, or worse yet losing, an item.
